pcs.pc_description: Procure full details of the shipment like item description, value, restrictions - import, export, transport, weight, dimensions, handling instructions, purpose, etc.
Collect transit details like origin, destination, clearance hub, incoterms, port of clearance, expected date of shipment etc.
Check with the customer (shipper/ receiver) if there are any additional requirements on transport and the budget allocated.
Gather details of transporters currently available and their cost, transit time, mode, VAS, etc.
Collect data on the newest improvements in transportation and BDP of leading market players.
Gather data on dwelling times and demurrage fees involved in all modes of transportation.

• Coordinate with stakeholders and collect the following information: • Regularity of similar shipments • Requirement of setting up a standard route/ network. • Possible bottlenecks • Issues faced in the past.
Research the documentation requirements and the preparation time.
Gather details on the restrictions/ approvals involved in each mode of transport and TAT for procuring the same.
Confirm the availability of existing transport routes, operators and options currently followed for such shipments.
Collect data on the availability of multimodal terminals with transhipment, loading/ unloading facilities, where the mode of transport can be changed.
Check the pre-haul and post-haul costs.
Collect data separately about operating costs in a single mode of transport for rail, road, air and inland waterways.
Check on the approximate transit time taken if a single mode of transport is used for rail, road, air and inland waterways.
Calculate the amount of coordination and intervention required for each leg of transportation.
Research the connecting hubs and routes for each mode of transport and each service provider.
Check the availability of direct booking software and the tracking number generation for each mode.
Check the FOIS portal for freight rates for rail transportation and the process of issuing the Railway Receipt and eT-TRR.
Collect data about rates from direct carrier portals.
Procure quotes from several vendors and explore options according to the time constraints.
Analyse the collected data and prepare the list of requirements and limitations.
Prepare a table with multimodal and intermodal transport costs, transit time, documentation, facilitation etc., with pros & cons.
Compare the transit time, cost, demurrage, transhipment cost, documentation, transit network data and quotes received from vendors.
Compare the difference in cost and services if booked directly with a carrier with that of transport service providers.

Check for the USPs from different carriers and analyse the tracking methods; devices used by them are of the latest technology like Radio frequency identification (RFID)-based tracking methods; and Internet of Things (IoT) telematics device-based tracking methods.
Coordinate with docking/transhipment terminals to know about space bookings, demurrage, facilities offered like forklift, crane etc. rental charges and restrictions if any.

pcs.pc_description: Prepare a map with the set of routes available with multimodal transport options and according to cost, transit time etc.
Compare routes taking the factors of freight analysis into consideration.
Prepare multiple route options according to the urgency, type of shipment and budget allotted.
Research and finalise vendors for establishing pre- and post-haulage processes.
Negotiate and plan for long-term contracts (LTC) with the airlines, transporters etc.
Check the FOIS portal for freight registration and other services for rail transportation.
Create separate plans for pre-haul, long-haul and end-haul transportation.
Use cost-effective transport like rail and inland waterways for long-haul transportation.

Give preference to vendors/ carriers who offer key aspects like low cost, high service levels & on- time deliveries, sustainability offerings, scalability and dedicated options, and technology first approach.
Arrange and plan for the Facility Location for transhipment and the MHE and labour required for the same.
Set Vendor KPIs, Payment methods while signing contracts. E.g., KPIs such as Delays, Rejections, Shortages, and Damages will be highlighted in the Vendor KPI dashboards.
Prepare multiple route plans with location, network design, scheduling, transportation, fleet renewal, resource allocation, schedule recovery and routing.
List the possible Tactical/strategic problems that may arise before finalising and create SOPs accordingly.
Finalize carriers, who have multimodal transport options as a single carrier (single-contract mode) with proper escalation matrix.
Decide docking methods to be followed based on the analysis done.
Create route plans based on hub and spoke methods.
Check on implementing CTD – combined transport document across networks for a single shipment.
Design multiple routes for multimodal transportation with different parameters like distance, transit time, cost, split transport, intermodal transport etc.

Set up an end-to-end process for the routes designed, roght from pick up to delivery, for each leg of transportation (including stuffing, stowing, repacking, loading, labelling, storing between transhipment, safety and security of load, etc.)
Do trial runs on each network designed and analyse efficiency based on parameters.

Create routes and plan for reverse logistics for the movement of trackable transport assets related to their reuse, recall, repair, repackaging and recycling, and return of goods delivered or empty containers back to the transport asset owner.

pcs.pc_description: Collect complete data of the shipment, including weight, value, type, dimensions, urgency, incoterms, documentation, date of arrival/ transport, origin, destination etc.
Prepare route plans with the networks set up, depending upon the transit time and budget allotted for the shipment.
Check space availability and the cost for different modes of transport.
Collect information about current situations, contingencies like congestion in ports, weather conditions etc. which might affect transit.
Decide on aspects like nearest hubs. It is not necessary that major hubs or gateways be used at all times.
Discuss with the consignee/ stakeholders about the available route options with ETA, cost and other possible hurdles.
Once the route is finalised, book space for each mode of transport using the concerned transport provider's software.
Plan Alternative and additional Transport Corridors according to Customer Needs.
Ensure that Infrastructure and Equipment at transit or connecting point are available.
Confirm that the Operation of cargo / Transshipment at the Transit point is handled according to the customs process.
Make sure that the goods are packed per the transit, transporter, customs etc. requirements and the transit documents, like the Airway bill are fixed properly on the package.
Ensure that the rules and regulations of transhipment according to the ports, transiting hubs, and customs are met while transporting and handling the cargo.
Assess the risks of Political situations, Port Congestion, Strikes, Riot, Backlog of common carriers, unforeseen costs from special handling etc.
Select the Strongest Agents in the planned Corridors.
Prepare transport documents according to the carriers, e.g., contract of carriage, bill of lading etc.
Ensure that tracking devices are added to the shipment and tracking is possible during the entire transit.
Confirm that proper repacking and consolidation happens when switching between modes of transport.
Organize manpower and storage space across disparate facilities.
Use navigational tools integrated with data from weather stations, satellites etc. for analyzing real-time traffic.
Analyse the demand patterns, wait times and historical records to improve efficiency.

Integrate existing transport management systems with AI-powered monitoring tools that identify potential dangers, such as accidents or obstructions, and send automated alerts with alternatives for prompt action.
Ensure cost efficiency by optimising the route and reducing the distance a shipment travels, resulting in less fuel consumption and reduced maintenance costs.

pcs.pc_description: Consolidate all the data of the shipment like the various carriers, routes, modes of transport, contact information of the carriers and stakeholders, ETA etc.

• Collect complete tracking identifiers listed below from carriers: • Transport contract identifiers such as waybills or consignment notes. • Transport means identifiers (e.g., IMO vessel number or truck license plate). • Transport equipment identifiers (e.g., shipping container/ULD/rail car IDs). • Transport movement identifiers (e.g., voyage number or flight); and • Identifier of all cargo carried by a transporter means for a specific transport movement (i.e., manifest).
Check the current status of the consignment using online tracking tools and match it with the master-level identifiers.
Check whether the status is getting updated at regular intervals.
Confirm whether the consignment is progressing as scheduled, and the event milestones are reached.
Check whether the physical handling of the shipment is happening as per the process.

• If the consignment is delayed, coordinate with the carrier, check the below, and document the same: • Reason for delay? • Whether the issue can be resolved? • When will the shipment move? • Will the ETA get impacted?
If the status of the shipment is not updated in the tracking system, raise a complaint with the carrier about the same.
Check for the last transit point updated and contact the concerned hub directly to know the status.
Regularly follow up with the concerned department of transportation/ carrier/ handler/ driver etc., for the current status of the shipment and match that with the same of online tracking.
In case of a tracking device fixed in the consignment, check for its status online at regular intervals.
Monitor the shipment on both master level and unit level and check whether the status of both matches.
Keep all the stakeholders informed about the status of the shipment and additional information about any changes in the transit time, exigencies etc.

pcs.pc_description: If the shipment is reported as damaged by the carrier during transit, collect the photos and inform the carrier to examine the extent of damage.
In case of tertiary damage, i.e., only the outer packing is damaged, coordinate with the carrier/ stakeholder to repack the shipment for further transit and record the incident accordingly.

In the scenario of the primary or secondary packing being damaged and the contents of the shipment being intact, coordinate with the shipper/ consignee on the next steps and whether the shipment will be accepted with repacking.
If the shipper/ consignee is not fine with further connecting the repacked shipment, coordinate with the carrier for having the shipment returned to origin or stored till further instruction.
If the complete shipment is damaged, including the contents, coordinate with the stakeholders/ shipper/ consignee for further instructions/ repair/ return/ scrap etc.
File for insurance or claim according to the SOP signed with carrier and perform root cause analysis if required
If the shipment status is not updated for more than 24 hours, the lost shipment process must be followed.
Initiate the searching process and check with the last updated hub for status updates.
Once the shipment status is received, coordinate with the carrier for the status to be updated in tracking software.
Collect information about the tracking device used and check data on its direct interface.
Check manually with the direct transporter like driver, loader etc. for the status of shipment and whether the tracking device is faulty or needs to be charged, replaced etc.

If the shipment has left a transit hub and has not reached the next hub/ station, track it with transport equipment identifiers (e.g., shipping container number/ULD/rail car IDs). If the status is available, wait for the container/ ULD to reach the next station and coordinate with them for the individual status of the shipment.

If the shipment is still untraceable with the master tracking IDs, start the manual searching process of individually coordinating with the ground- level staff like drivers, loaders, cargo handlers at transshipment hubs etc.
Check for CCTV footage, lost and found hub, unlabeled shipments, etc., as per the SOP set up with the carriers.
Check with the consignee whether the shipment is delivered or reached the destination without the tracking details being updated.
Register complaints according to the carrier's SOP and the contracts signed with them.
In case of the shipment declared as lost, File for insurance or claim according to the SOP signed with carrier and perform root cause analysis if required.
Consider a shipment under transit delay if it does not move as scheduled, and eventually, the ETA is affected or postponed.
If the shipment deviates from the route assigned or is found to be travelling past the destination, follow the steps mentioned below.

Investigate with the carrier why the shipment has not moved as planned and if the reason is found due to negligence by carrier/ handler, e.g., lack of loaders/ MHE, space constraints due to failed bookings, infrastructure failures etc.
Escalate the situation according to the SOP/ matrix received from the carrier and file for a claim if required.
Ensure that the shipment is connected through the next possible connection.
If the shipment is stuck for customs clearance, check with the CHA or the carrier coordinating with the reason for the hold and if any additional paperwork is required for clearance.

In the case of the shipment being delayed due to uncontrollable scenarios from the customs end, like physical inspection, congestion at the port, change of officers, revision of acts etc., keep the shipper, consignee and other stakeholders informed.
Plan for the next connection according to the anticipated clearance date and inform the next carrier.

If the transit is delayed due to unforeseen circumstances like natural disasters, War/ like operations, technical failures/ vehicle breakdowns/ epidemics, strikes, government directions or force majeure, etc., check with the current carrier/ handler for safe storage of the shipment and the cost for the same.
If the delay is more than anticipated and the situation remains unclear, coordinate with the shipper, consignee/ stakeholders etc., for the next plan of action.

If the shipment is delayed due to Accidents, road construction, inclement weather enroute, road debris, rush-hour congestion etc., check with the carrier on next plan for compensating the loss of transit time and update the stakeholders accordingly.

pcs.pc_description: Perform spending analysis with all forward and reverse costs considered.
Populate data from different software like TMS, fuel purchasing systems, truckload carrier accounting systems, customs, bill of lading data, and any others.
Collect trucking spot freight rates, contracted freight trends, current truck equipment orders, and outbound and inbound data.
Compare findings to industry trends.
Prepare a scorecard and use the same for easy comparison of carrier performances based on different factors.
Substantiate findings using facts-based analysis and quantification of exposures.
Assess the effectiveness of business monitoring procedures and processes.
Shift from stagnant or point-in-time reviews to focused implementation of ongoing monitoring.
Analyse company stock and location data for optimal routing.
Identify ways to optimise "less than truckload" shipments. Inefficient truck utilisation leads to revenue leaks.
The capacity of freight vessels and trains should be utilised at least at a rate of over 70% per trip in order to maintain profitability.
Identify high-risk business areas, products, freight carriers, business lines, and geographies to focus efforts.
Analyse overall freight expenses to identify anomalies.
Utilise available infrastructure to the maximum.
Collate data from tracing and analyse the same for patterns on transit time, delays and service failures.
Allocate full capacities to orders, and plan transportation itineraries and frequency.
Provide insights to the management by developing a deeper understanding of freight expenses to identify opportunities for improvement with (efficiency and control environment).
Use a route optimisation solution to optimise delivery routes around changing traffic conditions.
Use a transportation planning solution that integrates supply chain planning and shipping execution to assess real-time risk across the supply chain.
Integrate a shipment planning window with TMS that covers projection for several days forward and order management, procurement, and supply chain optimisation solutions.
Use technologies like weatheroptics to forecast and enhance the solutions for risks related to weather conditions. This allows rerouting of vehicles to minimize the impact of weather hazards.
Choose carriers with better vehicle maintenance and safety records, which reduces the risk of transit delays due to vehicle breakdowns.
Integrate digital freight markets and brokerages into TMS, which will help optimise cost and analyse the quotes.

Choose vendors with APIs for posting loads, booking, tendering, and tracking. Carriers using digital fleet management and TMS solutions with highly automated material handling reduce the risk of lost shipments.
Identify alternate ports and CFS/ ICDs, which decrease the risk of delay. Build agility into processes so that switch ports are available if needed.
